Alex / team —

Quick engineering breakdown based on the numbers Marissa shared and your SLOs. High level tradeoffs and an initial cost band (we'll put formal numbers into the spreadsheet Stef will attach):

Options to consider:
- Hosted (streaming):
  - Pros: fastest time-to-value, Redwood manages routing/scale, supports streaming out of the box.
  - Cons: slightly higher unit $/1M tokens due to streaming overhead and smaller batching windows.
  - Rough ballpark: $90–$140 / 1M tokens for streaming at volumes in the 100M–1B/month range depending on model and quantization.

- Hosted (batch/non-streaming):
  - Pros: lowest $/1M tokens — larger batch windows (100–300ms) can drive strong efficiency.
  - Cons: not ideal UX for token-by-token chat.
  - Rough ballpark: $50–$90 / 1M tokens with aggressive batching and caching.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Pros: predictable unit costs at scale, better for strict SLOs with isolation (can tune instance types and model variants).
  - Cons: commit required; higher up-front cost and ops coordination.
  - Rough ballpark (effective unit cost at 1B tokens/mo): $40–$70 / 1M tokens depending on commit level and model choice.

Latency vs batching guidance:
- For streaming UX + p95 <300ms we recommend a small batching window (15–40ms) and a streaming pipeline (continuous token flush). This keeps latency low but reduces batch efficiency.
- If you can accept p95 ~350–500ms, a 75–150ms batching window (or micro-batching on the client) materially reduces cost (~20–40%).

Initial recommendation for FinTechAI (based on your 6–12 mo ramp):
- Start on Hosted (streaming) to validate UX + surface issues quickly. Configure a small batch window (25–50ms) and enable prefix caching for common prompts.
- Prepare a dedicated reservation model to move to at ~500M–1B tokens/mo depending on cost targets.

I’ve attached a quick pricing estimate and two SLA options in the spreadsheet Marissa will send (redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx) — includes sample $/1M tokens at different batch windows and streaming vs batch rows.

—Rishi
